Reaccelerating inflation plus rising yields is precisely the tape that compresses rich multiples. Unemployment ticking up to 4.2% adds a mild stagflationary undertone. **Net regime read: constructive enough to hold and add selectively, but strongly biased toward valuation-protected names over expensive momentum.** This is exactly the logic behind my two existing holdings.

## 2. Portfolio review

Both positions were opened in the last ~24 hours, so this is a re-underwrite of very fresh theses.

**DELL — HOLD.** Cost 450.67, last 441.90 (−1.9%). Combined exposure ~$178 (~18% of $998 equity), both in servers_hardware. Cash $820. Room to add, but sector concentration and correlation are already meaningful in the one theme.

- **AMD** (top swing score 6.82) — strong, but forward P/E 41.6 / P/S 24 make it the most multiple-vulnerable large name in a rising-yield/reaccelerating-inflation tape, and earnings 8/4 (25 days) forces a swing to straddle a binary print. Not high-conviction asymmetric here. Watchlist.

Watchlist.
- **TXN** — earnings 7/22 (12 days) and EPS revisions turning *down*. Skip.
- **ANET / ALAB / CRDO / AMAT / WDC** — quality names but either richly valued into rising yields, extended, or near earnings. Watchlist.

The cheap, valuation-protected server names the regime favors are the two I *already own*, freshly deployed. Adding a third correlated server name or an expensive momentum name into a multiple-compressing tape is a mediocre setup — and the rules prefer nothing over mediocre.

## 5. Decision

**No new trades.** Hold DELL and HPE; re-underwrite next cycle.
